loaded.name: The Falklands War
loaded.description:
The Falklands War (1982) was a 74-day military conflict between Argentina and the UK over the Falkland Islands, South Georgia, and South Sandwich Islands in the South Atlantic. 

Argentina invaded the Falkland Islands on April 2, 1982, and the UK responded by sending a task force to retake the islands. The war ended on June 14, 1982, with Argentina's surrender and the islands' return to British control, resulting in the deaths of 649 Argentine, 255 British military personnel, and three Falkland Islanders.

subUnits.name: Workers
subUnits.description: The Argentine scrap metal workers, led by Constantino Davidoff, arrived at Leith Harbour on March 19, 1982, to dismantle an abandoned whaling station. By raising the Argentine flag and bypassing British customs at Grytviken, they triggered a diplomatic crisis. This unauthorized presence prompted the deployment of HMS Endurance, creating the immediate military friction that served as the final pretext for the Argentine invasion of the Falklands.

items.name: Maritime Exclusion Zone
items.description:
A [Maritime Exclusion Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maritime_Exclusion_Zone "Maritime Exclusion Zone") (MEZ) was declared on 12 April 1982 covered a circle of radius 200 nautical miles (370 km; 230 mi) from the centre of the Falkland Islands. Any *Argentine warship* or *naval auxiliary* entering the MEZ could have been attacked by [British nuclear-powered submarines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy_Submarine_Service "Royal Navy Submarine Service") (SSN).

From [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_Exclusion_Zone)

items.name: Corbeta Uruguay base
items.description:
**Corbeta Uruguay base** was an [Argentine military](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_of_Argentina "Military of Argentina") outpost established in November 1976 on [Thule Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thule_Island "Thule Island"), [Southern Thule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Thule "Southern Thule"), in the [South Sandwich Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sandwich_Islands "South Sandwich Islands"). It was vacated and mostly demolished in 1982 following Britain's victory against Argentina in the Falklands War.

From [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corbeta_Uruguay_base)

media.caption: The Corbeta Uruguay station on Southern Thule, 1981
media.credits: Ricardo A. R. Hermelo, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

items.name: Orcadas
items.description:
**Base Orcadas** is an [Argentine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina") scientific station in [Antarctica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctica "Antarctica"), and the oldest of the stations in Antarctica still in operation. It is located on [Laurie Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurie_Island "Laurie Island"), one of the [South Orkney Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Orkney_Islands "South Orkney Islands") ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): *Islas Orcadas del Sur*), at 4 meters (13 ft) above sea level and 170 meters (558 ft) from the coastline.

From [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orcadas_Base)

loaded.name: Northern Storm 1985
loaded.description:
> **AI-generated scenario.** This scenario was created with an AI model and has not been reviewed for historical accuracy. Treat the orders of battle, locations and details as illustrative only. It is meant to test and showcase the features of ORBAT Mapper.

**Fictional scenario**, inspired by Tom Clancy's *Red Storm Rising* (1986).

June 1985. With its oil industry crippled, the Soviet Union decides to seize the Persian Gulf, and first to defeat NATO in Europe. The Red Army attacks across the inner German border, an airborne regiment seizes Iceland, and Backfire bombers and submarines strike at the carriers and convoys bringing American reinforcements across the Atlantic.

The scenario covers land, air, sea and subsurface forces from 6 to 21 June 1985. Unit designations, garrisons and equipment follow the mid-1980s orders of battle. The events, timings and losses are invented.

June 1985. With its oil industry crippled, the Soviet Union decides to seize the Persian Gulf, and first to defeat NATO in Europe. The Red Army attacks across the inner German border, an airborne regiment seizes Iceland, and Backfire bombers and submarines strike at the carriers and convoys bringing American reinforcements across the Atlantic.

The scenario covers land, air, sea and subsurface forces from 6 to 21 June 1985. Unit designations, garrisons and equipment follow the mid-1980s orders of battle. The events, timings and losses are invented.

events.title: Moscow decides
events.description: Months after saboteurs wrecked the oil complex at Nizhnevartovsk, the Politburo concludes that only the Persian Gulf can cover the shortfall, and that NATO must be knocked out of the war first. A peace initiative in Vienna gives cover for the build-up.

events.title: NATO alert
events.description: Intelligence picks up the movement of Soviet divisions out of their barracks. NORTHAG and CENTAG move to their general defence plan positions.

events.title: Reinforcement convoys at sea
events.description: Convoy RF-1 is five days out of Norfolk. The Striking Fleet Atlantic gathers south of the Faroes.

events.title: Airlift leaves Pskov
events.description: An airborne regiment boards Il-76s for a long flight around the North Cape.

events.title: H-hour: the Red Army attacks
events.description: Four armies cross the inner German border on a front from the Baltic to the Thuringian Forest.

events.title: Iceland seized
events.description: Airborne troops land at Keflavík while a Soviet merchant ship unloads armour in Reykjavík. The surviving F-15s and P-3s escape to Scotland.

events.title: Backfires strike the Striking Fleet
events.description: Two naval missile regiments launch more than a hundred Kh-22s. Foch is sunk and Nimitz damaged.

events.title: Elbe bridges dropped
events.description: F-111Fs drop the bridges at Dömitz and Wittenberge.
